writingRules.template:
# Writing rules

These rules are checked against every page by the Folio assistant ("Check against writing rules") and shown to external agents before they write. Edit them to match your team: keep each rule short, give it a name, and say what to do instead.

## Plain language
Use short, common words and active voice. Prefer "use" to "utilize" and "start" to "commence". Write for a colleague who joined this week.

## One idea per paragraph
A paragraph makes one point, in at most four sentences. Split a paragraph that does two jobs.

## Headings are nouns
Name a section by its subject ("Deployment", "Access rules"), not by a sentence or a question. Keep heading levels in order and never skip one.

## No marketing words
Drop "seamless", "powerful", "robust", "cutting-edge", "revolutionary" and similar claims. State what the thing does, with a number or an example when you have one.

## Define acronyms on first use
Spell out an acronym the first time it appears on a page, with the short form in brackets: "single sign-on (SSO)". Skip this for ones the whole team uses daily.

## Steps are numbered and start with a verb
Write a procedure as a numbered list. Each step is one action: "Open Settings", "Click Save". Put the expected result after the step it belongs to.

## Concrete over vague
Replace "soon", "a few", "some" and "various" with dates, numbers or names. Link to the source instead of repeating it.

## Consistent terms
Use one name for one thing. If the team calls it a "space", do not call it a "workspace" on the next line.
